translations.answer: The core distinction of the thread is that stack allocation typically involves only known pointer adjustments and is not necessarily problematic when local variables are present; default heap allocation lacks inherent determinism. Auditing should focus on the construction, resize, string/container members, and smart pointers of each local object, rather than merely searching for local variable declarations. Special attention should be given to logging and std::make_shared, which must be verified to enter deterministic read/update/write paths. The thread does not provide evidence that the entire codebase has been cleaned, so it can only be used as an audit method and not as a real-time validation result.
translations.applicability: Applicable to ros2_control and other systems requiring deterministic WBC read/update/write loops; the thread corresponds to the 2022 code snapshot, and the current version requires re-audit.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for the environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: The thread discussed pre-allocating a sufficiently large buffer and using TLSF to determine the allocator.
translations.details.attempts.1: The selection of joint_trajectory_controller was based on joint_names_.size() as the command length upper bound, and pre-allocated before the real-time loop.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Auditing each local object for its construction, resize, string/container members, and smart pointers, rather than merely searching for local variable declarations.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Auditing logging and std::make_shared to ensure they enter deterministic read/update/write paths.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: If using a deterministic allocator, the initialization of the object itself must also be deterministic.
translations.details.environments.0: The thread references ros2_control commit 6b495ef86889cbfdc1ee22ac77efa2ff589727ee in actuator.cpp and ros2_controllers commit b9ccf04aa95203e37077f297ddcf9f933ef464fa in joint_trajectory_controller.cpp.
translations.details.limits.0: Stack allocation is typically O(1), but this does not imply that any class's construction is heap-based; it must be reviewed class by class.
translations.details.limits.1: TLSF addresses only part of the determinism of the allocator; the original response explicitly warns about the initialization logic as well.
translations.details.limits.2: The thread does not provide delayed histograms, worst-case execution times, or hard-real-time validation data.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Project members agree that some parts of the codebase require cleanup, but the Issue does not provide evidence that the entire codebase has been audited or merged with fixes.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The Issue was closed by a stale bot in 2025, with the reason being inactivity, not technical remediation validation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Declaring local variables in real-time update/write loops may necessarily disrupt determinism; how to identify true dynamic allocation?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: A true real-time WBC should not assume 'pre-allocated' satisfies hard real-time without measurement in target load, scheduling, and logging configuration.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Equating 'declaring local variables' with 'dynamic heap allocation' misses the determinism difference between the two.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The real risk comes from internal container expansion, default heap allocation, logging, and shared pointer construction, all of which are unpredictable at execution time.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The update() function declares three JointTrajectoryPoint, then calls resize_joint_trajectory_point based on joint_names_.size().
translations.details.symptoms.1: The same thread also identifies deterministic paths with logging and std::make_shared.
